scope: Selected claims in the proposed 72-shot Nokia review cut. The narrative, graphics, implied dates, causal interpretations, and final title have not been exhaustively checked.

claims.claim: Nokia traces its origins to an 1865 wood-pulp mill and another mill by the Nokianvirta River.

sources.support: Nokia's history describes Fredrik Idestam's 1865 wood-pulp mill in southern Finland and a second mill on the Nokianvirta River.
Nokia identifies its 1865 founding on the Tammerkoski rapids in Tampere.

claims.claim: Nokia Corporation resulted from a merger of Nokia AB, Finnish Rubber Works, and Finnish Cable Works in 1967.

sources.support: Nokia's 2004 Form 20-F, item 4.A, names all three companies and dates the merger to 1967.

claims.claim: Nokia's Mobira Cityman was a handportable phone in 1987.

sources.support: Nokia's history media library captions Mobira Cityman as an NMT900 handportable in 1987.

claims.claim: The first official GSM call in Helsinki was made in 1991 using Nokia equipment.

sources.support: Nokia dates the official call to 1 July 1991 in Helsinki and describes the car-phone call.
Nokia's history states that a Nokia phone and its Radiolinja network were used in 1991.

claims.claim: The Nokia 1011 appeared in 1992 and was an early mass-produced GSM phone.

sources.support: Nokia dates its first GSM cell phone, the 1011, to late 1992.
The Science Museum Group dates its 1011 object 1992–1994 and describes it as a mass-produced GSM phone.
The Mobile Phone Museum dates its announcement to 10 November 1992.

claims.claim: Nokia refocused on telecommunications in the early 1990s and divested non-telecommunications businesses over several years.

sources.support: The 2004 Form 20-F describes the early-1990s strategic focus and dates the divestitures to 1989–1996, not all to 1992.
This timeline associates the 1992 strategic decision with Jorma Ollila. Check the precise dating against primary board records before release.

claims.claim: The Nokia 3210 was announced in 1999 and had an integrated antenna and customizable covers.

sources.support: The museum dates its announcement to 18 March 1999 and describes the integrated antenna and Xpress-on covers; it also disputes widely circulated lifetime sales numbers, which this cut does not use.

claims.claim: The Nokia 3310 was introduced in 2000 and became associated with Snake and durability.

sources.support: The Guardian labels the 3310 as a 2000 phone, says it had Snake 2, and describes its reputation for indestructibility elsewhere in the gallery.

claims.claim: Gartner estimated Nokia at 37.8% of worldwide end-user sales of all mobile phones in full-year 2007, close to 40%.

sources.support: The reproduced Gartner full-year all-mobile table gives Nokia 37.8%, Motorola 14.3%, Samsung 13.4%, Sony Ericsson 8.8%, and LG 6.8%.
Nokia separately estimated 40% of device sales in Q4 2007; do not mix that quarter with Gartner's full-year end-user estimate.

claims.claim: Gartner's estimates put Nokia's share of all mobile-phone sales at 37.8% in 2007, 36.4% in 2009, 23.8% in 2011, 19.1% in 2012 and 13.9% in 2013.
claims.location: s01-08 and s09-03 charts; annual end-user all-mobile sales, not smartphone share

sources.support: Gartner's 2007 all-mobile table gives Nokia 37.8%.
The Gartner table gives Nokia 36.4% in 2009.
Gartner's full-year table gives 23.8% in 2011 and 19.1% in 2012.
Table 4 gives Nokia 13.9% of all mobile phones sold in full-year 2013.

claims.claim: Symbian accounted for 63.5% of full-year 2007 smartphone OS sales in Gartner's data, approximately two thirds.

sources.support: This secondary reproduction of Gartner's full-year 2007 smartphone OS table reports Symbian 63.5%, RIM 9.6%, Windows Mobile 12.0%, Mac OS X 2.7% and other systems totaling 12.1%; retrieve a primary table if possible.

claims.claim: Gartner's full-year Android share of smartphone OS sales increased from 3.9% in 2009 to 78.4% in 2013, with intervening bars of 22.7%, approximately 46%, and 66.4%.

sources.support: Gartner's archived February 2011 table gives 3.9% for 2009 and 22.7% for 2010; archive access should be checked.
Computerworld independently reports the same two Gartner shares.
The Guardian gives about 219m of 472m smartphone shipments in 2011, rounded in the chart to roughly 46%; the article separately reports 50.9% for Q4, not the year.
Gartner table 3 gives Android 66.4% in 2012 and 78.4% in 2013.

claims.claim: Steve Jobs introduced the original iPhone in San Francisco on 9 January 2007.

sources.support: Apple's contemporaneous Macworld San Francisco announcement is dated January 9, 2007 and describes its multitouch display.

claims.claim: Google acquired Android in 2005, announced Android and the Open Handset Alliance in 2007, and the first production Android phone was announced in 2008.

sources.support: Reuters says Google acquired Android in 2005; the price was undisclosed.
The 2007 contemporaneous report describes the Android and Open Handset Alliance announcement.
The museum describes the T-Mobile G1 / HTC Dream as the first production Android phone, announced 23 September 2008.

claims.claim: Stephen Elop became Nokia CEO in 2010; Nokia and Microsoft announced a proposed Windows Phone partnership in February 2011.

sources.support: Nokia's Q3 2010 interim report records Elop's appointment as president and CEO effective September 21, 2010.
The companies' announcement is dated 11 February 2011 and says Windows Phone would be Nokia's principal smartphone strategy; the term sheet was initially non-binding.

claims.claim: An internal Elop memo in February 2011 used a burning-platform metaphor.

sources.support: BBC reported the memo in February 2011 and said it verified that the memo was genuine.
Engadget published the memo and described its confirmation by sources.

claims.claim: Microsoft and Nokia announced a €5.44bn transaction in September 2013; the announced amount included €3.79bn for the business and €1.65bn for a patent license. The sale closed in April 2014.

sources.support: The 3 September announcement gives the two euro components and says Nokia would retain its patent portfolio.
Reuters described the announced €5.44bn as approximately $7.2bn at the time.
Nokia announced completion on 25 April 2014; the 2013 announcement and closing are different events.

claims.claim: Nokia finalized its acquisition of Alcatel-Lucent in 2016.

sources.support: Nokia's release says it finalized the acquisition on 2 November 2016, following combined operations from January.

open_issues: Coverage is partial: all remaining words and every on-screen statement, chart denominator, period, and causal interpretation still require independent review.

The opening says billions of people carry Nokia products; source and time-bound this claim or propose a narrower replacement. The 2011 partnership announcement cites 1.3 billion daily users, not a timeless plural figure.
Touchscreens replaced buttons is rhetorical shorthand; check or soften it before release because smartphones still have physical controls.

The original $300 billion title is not approved: Reuters describes a peak market value close to $300bn but does not establish the precise date or calculation here; the replacement title is proposed, not approved.
Check the 1992 timing of Nokia's strategic decision against primary corporate records and replace any weak or unavailable sources.
Visual handset drawings are stylized, not product photographs. Check every shot for accurate and relevant representation.
A human must check source access, context, narration, captions, music and the ending in the actual final render.
